action.headline: The city can buy vacant buildings that don't sell at court-ordered auctions.
action.what_changed: This bill was reintroduced in 2025 after an identical version (21-0114) failed at the end of the council term in 2021. Eight of the original sponsors returned to support it. The current version has been enacted.
action.why_it_matters: When a court appoints a receiver to sell a problem vacant building and no one bids at the public auction, the receiver currently has limited options. This law gives the city the right to purchase those properties at a capped price, potentially allowing the city to control what happens to buildings that the private market won't buy.
